## Introduction

State the review question and why it matters. Define the scope: which years,
venues and kinds of study are included.

## Background

Give the reader the minimum context needed to follow the themes. Cite the
foundational works here, not every paper in the matrix.

## Themes

### Theme one

Make one comparative claim about this group of papers. Cite the works that
support it and name the disagreement where there is one.

### Theme two

Repeat for the second theme. Prefer synthesis over a sequence of paper
summaries.

## Synthesis

Bring the themes together. What does the body of work agree on, and where does
the evidence conflict?

## Gaps

State the gap precisely enough that a study could address it. Distinguish
"nobody has looked" from "the available studies are too weak to decide".

## Conclusion

Restate the review's contribution in two or three sentences.
